title: 结语：一个只有众人而无人民的世界
originalTitle: Conclusion: A World of People without a People

zh: 要问人们最应该把什么归功于那些被称为资本家的人奉行的道德实践，答案是：他们的生命本身。
en: If we ask what men most owe to the moral practices of those who are called capitalists the answer is: their very lives.

zh: ——弗里德里希·A.·哈耶克，1989年
en: —Friedrich A. Hayek, 1989

zh: 柏林墙倒塌两年之后、苏联正式解体前一个月，乔治·H. W. 布什把总统自由勋章授予了威廉·勒普克（Röpke）的通信者、美国南方种族隔离制度的捍卫者威廉·F. 巴克利（William F. Buckley）。布什声称，巴克利“提升了这个国家政治辩论的水准”。他浑然不觉其中的讽刺，随后又把一枚勋章授予一位民权运动领袖。当天最后一枚勋章授予了九十二岁的F. A. 哈耶克。布什说：“我们向哈耶克致敬，致敬他一生眺望地平线之外。在许多人视社会主义为历史天命之时，他预见了自由的胜利……冯·哈耶克教授被中东欧的自由人民尊崇为一位真正的远见卓识者，也被全世界公认为思想与政治领域中的革命者。亲眼目睹自己的理念在世界面前得到验证，对他而言该是何等壮美。”
在这个本就极富讽刺的一天里，又添一重讽刺：这个认为自己的核心发现乃是世界、未来与人类心智之根本不可知的人，如今竟因其近乎神秘的先见之明而受到褒扬。
en: Two years after the fall of the Berlin Wall and one month short of the official dissolution of the Soviet Union, George H. W. Bush granted a Presidential Medal of Freedom to Wilhelm Röpke’s correspondent and the defender of racial segregation in the U.S. South, William F. Buckley. Buckley had “raised the level of political debate in this country,” Bush claimed. Without irony, he followed by granting a medal to a civil rights leader. The last medal of the day was offered to the ninety-two-year-old F. A. Hayek. “We honor” Hayek, Bush said, “for a lifetime of looking beyond the horizon. At a time when many saw socialism as ordained by history, he foresaw freedom’s triumph. … Professor von Hayek is revered by the free people of Central and Eastern Europe as a true visionary, and recognized worldwide as a revolutionary in intellectual and political thought. How magnificent it must be for him to witness his ideas validated before the eyes of the world.”

In another irony on a day already rich with them, the man who saw his central discovery to be the fundamental unknowability of the world, the future, and the human mind was now being honored for his near-mystical foresight.

zh: 布什演说中隐含的冷战胜利主义同样具有讽刺意味，因为冷战对哈耶克而言几乎无足轻重。在他卷帙浩繁的著述中，这场冲突几乎了无踪影。有一处意味深长的例外：1979年他谈到美国对外援助，说它由于“与俄国的愚蠢竞争”而在“大规模补贴不发达国家的社会主义实验”。
更耐人寻味的一段引文出自他的著作《自由秩序原理》（The Constitution of Liberty），他写道：“表面看来，似乎今天有两种文明正在争夺世界人民的效忠，但事实是，它们向大众许诺的前景、向大众提供的实惠，本质上是相同的。”
双方都想要繁荣，也都想要借助国家的帮助来重新分配繁荣。哈耶克写道：“随着有关种种可能性的知识比物质利益本身传播得更快，今天世界上很大一部分人民不满的程度前所未有，并决意夺取他们视为自身权利的东西。随着他们力量的增长，他们将有能力强行实现这种再分配。”
当然，世界人民用来“强行”索取再分配的手段将是民主，而其力量增长的路径则是非殖民化。在新自由主义的世纪里，相对于大众获得选举权与帝国终结这条主线，冷战只是一段插曲。
en: The implicit Cold War triumphalism of Bush’s speech was also ironic considering how little the Cold War meant to Hayek. In his voluminous writings, the conflict scarcely appears. In one telling exception, he referred in 1979 to American foreign aid, which was “subsidizing on a large scale the socialist experiments of underdeveloped countries” because of a “silly competition with Russia.”
An even more telling quote comes from his book

where he wrote: “While superficially it may seem that two types of civilization are today competing for the allegiance of the people of the world, the fact is that the promise they offer to the masses, the advantages they hold out to them, are essentially the same.”

Both sides wanted prosperity and they wanted the state’s help to redistribute it. “With the knowledge of possibilities spreading faster than the material benefits,” Hayek wrote, “a great part of the people of the world are today dissatisfied as never before and are determined to take what they regard as their rights. As their strength grows, they will become able to extort such a redistribution.”

Of course, the means the people of the world would use to “extort” redistribution would be democracy, and the way their strength would grow was through decolonization. In the neoliberal century, the Cold War was a sideshow to the main event of the rise of mass enfranchisement and the end of empire.

zh: 哈耶克把《自由秩序原理》题献给“正在美国成长中的那个未知文明”。本书所描述的这些新自由主义者所设想的未知文明，有何基本特征？它必然是全球性的，其制度设计旨在遏制获得民主权能的大众可能带来的扰动。那是一个没有帝国的世界，但规则由超国家机构制定，而这些机构的运作处于任何选民都鞭长莫及之处。在那个世界里，全球经济被稳妥地保护起来，免受再分配平等与社会正义之要求的冲击。我的叙述勾勒了一条线索，从哈布斯堡帝国的终结通往世界贸易组织的建立。在柏林墙倒塌前夕，新自由主义的主要刊物《秩序》（Ordo）上，勒普克的外甥汉斯·维尔格罗德特（Hans Willgerodt）对这个秩序全球主义的世纪作出了精当的总结。在援引哈耶克与罗宾斯1930年代的著述之后，他写道，“作为共产主义在国际上宣告破产的见证人”，民族国家现在该认识到，它们“过度使用了自己主权”。
他写道，19世纪通过“经济领域的根本性去政治化”实现了“世界经济一体化”。
他援引勒普克1952年的话，附和后者的观点：“如果联合国授予发展中国家征收外国财产的权利，那么这意味着，一旦它们行使这样一种‘权利’，它们就不仅脱离了世界市场……而且[把自己]逐出了文明国家的国际法律共同体。”
en: Hayek dedicated

to “the unknown civilization that is growing in America.” What were the parameters of the unknown civilization envisaged by the neoliberals described in these pages? It was necessarily global, designed with institutions to contain potential disruptions from the democratically empowered masses. It was a world without empires but with rules set by supranational bodies operating beyond the reach of any electorate. It was a world where the global economy was safely protected from the demands of redistributive equality and social justice. My narrative has traced a line that leads from the end of the Habsburg Empire to the foundation of the World Trade Organization. In the leading neoliberal journal

on the eve of the fall of the Berlin Wall, Röpke’s nephew Hans Willgerodt offered a fine summation of the century of ordoglobalism. After citing Hayek and Robbins’s writings from the 1930s, he wrote that “as witnesses of the international declaration of bankruptcy by communism,” it was time that nation-states realized they had “made too much use of their sovereignty.”
He wrote that the nineteenth century had achieved “world economic integration” through a “fundamental depoliticization of the economic domain.”

Quoting Röpke from 1952, he echoed Röpke’s sentiment that if “the developing countries are granted by the UN a right to expropriate foreign property, this means, when they make use of such a ‘right,’ they not only detach themselves from the world-economic market … but [take themselves] out of the international legal community of the civilized nations.”

zh: 论及通往世界经济一体化之路，维尔格罗德特既瞻前亦顾后：“诸如关贸总协定[GATT（General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade）]一类的机构，能够助推这条道路，即把世界市场从国家规制与贸易壁垒中解放出来的道路。”
但他也搬出了哈耶克与米塞斯的旧模板：中欧帝国。“一个对主权行使加以约束的国际法治，对于中央集权式民族国家的拥趸而言，无疑是一个困难而又陌生的观念。国家必须首先放弃对其公民的权威。它还必须向下与联邦结构分享主权，并向上在一个国际法律共同体之内约束自身。毫无疑问，国际秩序正朝着这个方向移动。正是在这一脉络中，必须重新检讨那种关于绵延长久的神圣罗马帝国秩序的扭曲评判。”
如此字面意义上的帝国怀旧实属罕见。不过，另一个著名的例外是朝圣山学社（MPS）主席迪帕克·拉尔（Deepak Lal）。受美国以自由民主之名入侵阿富汗与伊拉克的鼓舞，他于2004年撰写了一篇颂扬帝国之作，赞美帝国带来秩序、确立法治、“平息族群冲突”的能力。
文章开篇便称颂哈布斯堡帝国，痛陈“继承国普通公民所能获得的机会大为减少”。
en: For the road to world economic integration, Willgerodt looked both ahead and back: “The path to the liberation of the world market from national regulation and trade barriers can be facilitated by institutions like GATT [General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade].”

But he also invoked the old template of Hayek and Mises: Central European empire: “The international rule of law with curbed application of sovereignty is doubtless a difficult and unfamiliar idea for the proponents of centralist national states. The state must first forego authority over its citizens. It must also share its sovereignty downward with federal structures and bind itself upward within an international legal community. No doubt the international order is moving in this direction. It is in this context that the distorted judgment about the order of the long-lived Holy Roman Empire must be taken up again.”

Such literal nostalgia for empire was rare. Another notable exception, though, was Mont Pèlerin Society (MPS) president Deepak Lal, who, inspired by the U.S. invasion of Afghanistan and Iraq in the name of liberal democracy, wrote a paean to empire in 2004 for its ability to bring order, institute the rule of law, and “quell ethnic conflicts.”
He began by eulogizing the Habsburg Empire, condemning “the great deterioration of opportunities that has befallen the average citizen of the successor states.”

zh: 然而，大多数新自由主义者承认，民族国家的时代已不可逆转。他们梦想的是一种非殖民化，其中不夹杂拉尔所援引的那些中东欧继承国自身表现出来的、对经济自主的破坏性渴望。本书讲述了从1920年代到1990年代新自由主义的制度解决方案的故事，把它们看作捍卫世界经济、使之免受民主与民族主义冲击的制度尝试。对哈耶克、罗宾斯与米塞斯而言，这意味着双重政府的国际联邦蓝图：在赋予政治独立的同时，保全竞争的统治地位。对海尔佩林而言，这意味着那部失败的普世投资法典——它试图把法律置于国家之外。对勒普克与哈特而言，这意味着种种形式的种族隔离与加权投票权。对梅斯特马克而言，这意味着《罗马条约》以及紧随其后的竞争法。对图姆利尔与彼得斯曼而言，这意味着经过改造的关贸总协定——其司法管辖权可以伸入国家内部。
en: Most neoliberals, however, acknowledged that the era of the nation was irreversible. They dreamt of decolonization without the destructive desire for economic autonomy displayed by the very successor states of East Central Europe that Lal cited. This book has told stories of the neoliberal fix from the 1920s to the 1990s as institutional attempts to defend the world economy against democracy and nationalism. For Hayek, Robbins, and Mises, this meant blueprints for international federations of double government, granting political independence while preserving the reign of competition. For Heilperin, it was in the failed universal code of investment with its attempt to place law beyond the state. For Röpke and Hutt, it was forms of apartheid and weighted franchise. For Mestmäcker, it was the Treaty of Rome and the competition law that followed it. For Tumlir and Petersmann, it was the GATT reformed with a jurisdiction that reached into domestic states.

zh: 我已在书中论证，转向法律是德语世界的新自由主义在二战之后最重要的方向转变。我所谓的秩序全球主义促成了一种理解：欧洲经济共同体（EEC）以及后来的世界贸易组织（世贸组织），乃是一套套法权装置，以法律围封市场，使其超出民主问责的范围，与此同时却又试图通过向民族国家之外的公民直接赋予私人权利来制造正当性。值得注意的是，随着秩序自由主义的注意力转向全球或国际尺度，他们曾经大加标榜的对分配性国家诸面向的包容便消失不见。
国际劳工组织（ILO）一类把工人权利与社会正义纳入自身使命的机构，再度成为敌人。
就在勒普克于民族国家内部构想累进所得税与扩大私有财产的持有范围的同一时刻，他开出的国际秩序处方却是一整套约束。
除其他含义外，这再次表明：社会市场经济中的“社会”二字，与其说是其哲学核心面向的标志，不如说更多是向战后西德有组织的劳工力量与社会主义情绪的强势所作的一种策略性必要让步。
在民族国家之外——民主与有组织劳工的杠杆在那里更为乏力——“社会”的话语销声匿迹，只剩下规则。
en: I have argued that the turn to law was the most important reorientation of German-speaking neoliberalism after the Second World War. What I have called ordoglobalism helped produce an understanding of the European Economic Community (EEC) and later the World Trade Organization (WTO) as apparatuses of juridical power to encase markets beyond democratic accountability even as it sought to create legitimacy through offering direct private rights to citizens beyond the nation. It is notable that, in the shift of ordoliberal attention to the global or international scale, their much-vaunted inclusion of aspects of the distributive state disappears.
Institutions like the International Labour Organization (ILO) that made workers’ rights and social justice part of their mandate became the enemy again.
At the exact same time that Röpke was envisioning a progressive income tax and diffusion of private property within the nation, he was prescribing an international order of constraints.

Among other things, this shows again that the “social” in the social market economy might be seen more as a tactically necessary concession to the strength of organized labor and socialist sentiment in postwar West Germany than as an indication of a core aspect of their philosophy.
Beyond the nation—where the levers of democracy and organized labor are weaker—the language of the social disappeared, and only the rules remained.

zh: 学界为新自由主义的制度解决方案给出了各种名称。有人称之为“资本主义的宪法保护”。
有人称之为“哈耶克式经济宪法”，旨在“使不断扩张的资本主义市场不受干预型平等主义民主政治的影响”。
斯蒂芬·吉尔（Stephen Gill）以一个影响深远的造语称之为“新宪政主义”，它力求“让居支配地位的经济力量日益与民主统治和大众问责相隔绝”。
正如学者所概括，这种宪政化“搭建起一张全球性的制度之网，为跨国资本提供多重退出选项”。
en: Scholars have given various names to the neoliberal fix. One calls it the “constitutional protection of capitalism.”
Another calls it the “Hayekian economic constitution” aimed at the “immunization of expanding capitalist markets against egalitarian-interventionist democratic politics.”
In an influential coinage, Stephen Gill calls it the “New Constitutionalism” striving to “allow dominant economic forces to be increasingly insulated from democratic rule and popular accountability.”
As summarized by scholars, this constitutionalization “establishes a worldwide institutional grid that offers transnational capital multiple exit options.”

zh: 另有人以不同方式书写新自由主义的制度解决方案的历史。有学者写到港务机构中“非多数决”的治理模式以及中央银行独立性的理念。
还有人看到这一脉络体现在欧洲中央银行与欧盟的治理结构之中。
另有学者描述了由避税港构成的“离岸世界”的造就——各国在其中竞相提供尽可能低的企业税、尽可能大的保密性，并为个人与公司提供最好的激励，使其得以逃离自家再分配国家的钳制。
1990年代及其后的讨论，则被“区位竞争”与“政策竞争”的观念主导。
新自由主义国际秩序观念的根基，是所谓竞争性联邦主义的设想——资本得以跨境追随机会，无论机会在何处出现。在一项对新自由主义联邦主义的研究中，有学者指出美国企业研究所（AEI）于2000年设立了一个联邦主义项目（Federalism Project），延续布坎南（Buchanan）1990年代的建议，以维护“市场关系中的有效退出选项”。
该研究所的一位驻所学者这样解释这个项目的愿景：“一个没有边界的世界，就是一个没有出口的世界。我们需要出口。”
这些想象图景与新自由主义者据称信奉的无国界世界或零国家社会相去甚远。
本书所描述的种种，就没那么容易被打发成一厢情愿的幻想了。秩序全球主义所设想的双重世界更为现实，至少在理论上也更有可能实现。在这个世界中，统治权（imperium）与所有权（dominium）分立，市场受到制度的围封。
en: Others have written the history of the neoliberal fix in different ways. One scholar writes of the “nonmajoritarian” models of governance in port authorities and the idea of central bank independence.
Still others have seen this strain in the European Central Bank and the governance structure of the European Union.

Other scholars have described the creation of an “offshore world” of tax havens through which nations compete to offer the least possible corporate tax, the greatest possible secrecy, and the best incentives for individuals and corporations to flee the clutches of their own redistributive states.
Discussions in the 1990s and beyond have been dominated by “locational competition” and the idea of “policy competition.”

At the root of the neoliberal idea of international order is the notion of so-called competitive federalism, with the possibility of capital following opportunities across borders wherever they arise. In an exploration of neoliberal federalism, one scholar notes that the American Enterprise Institute set up a Federalism Project in 2000, pursuing Buchanan’s proposals from the 1990s to preserve “an effective exit option in market relationships.”
An AEI resident scholar explained the vision of the project: “A world without borders is a world without exits. We need the exits.”
These imaginaries are far from the borderless world or zero-state society in which neoliberals purportedly believed.

What has been described in these pages is much less easy to dismiss as a fanciful delusion. More realistic and, at least in theory, more realizable, is ordoglobalism’s vision of a doubled world: divided and encased between imperium and dominium.

zh: 我的叙述指出了哈耶克思想以及我所谓日内瓦学派（Geneva School）新自由主义核心的一个悖论。一方面，世界经济必须加以捍卫，以防民主的越界之举。另一方面，世界经济本身却是不可见的，超出理性所能理解和表述的范围。哈耶克说得很明白：全球市场——或他所说的“扩展秩序”——“唯一贴切的词”是“超越性的”。就其“字面意义”而言，世界市场“远远超出我们的理解、愿望与目的以及我们感官知觉之所及，它涵纳并生发出任何个体头脑或任何单一组织都不可能拥有或发明出来的知识”。
这种对世界经济的神圣化理解并不限于哈耶克。新自由主义最重要刊物的刊名“秩序”（Ordo）——秩序自由主义者之名即由此而来——源自中世纪神学。
哈耶克把圣奥古斯丁的对话录视为秩序概念的起点。

在这些讨论中，奥古斯丁指出，宇宙的非凡复杂性确确实实是任何一个个体都无法理解的。他不仅描述了人类面对这一更大秩序时必然产生的无力感，还描述了我们的个体主观视角所带来的扭曲。他写道：“情形好比一个人只能察看镶嵌地面的一小块，却又凑得太近去看，随后便责怪工匠不懂秩序与构图。”局部看似无序，实则是观者有限视角的产物——他“未能注意到那个更大的马赛克世界”，而这个世界“会聚为一幅美丽图画的统一整体”。努力追求更宏观视角的个体，始终冒着把无序误认作有序的风险——反之亦然。他写道，这些人“无法把握整个宇宙的和谐与相互作用，又为超出自己认知范围的事物所苦，于是轻率地断言事物本来就是丑陋而无序的”。
en: My narrative has pointed to a paradox at the heart of Hayek’s thought and what I have called Geneva School neoliberalism. On the one hand, the world economy had to be defended against the excesses of democracy. On the other hand, the world economy itself was invisible and beyond reason and representation. Hayek was explicit when he wrote that “the only appropriate word” for the global market, or what he calls “the extended order,” is “transcendent.” In “its literal meaning,” the world market “far surpasses the reach of our understanding, wishes and purposes, and our sense perceptions, and that which incorporates and generates knowledge which no individual brain, or any single organization, could possess or invent.”
This sacred understanding of the world economy is not limited to Hayek. The word
in the title of the most important journal of neoliberalism, and from which the ordoliberals take their name, comes from medieval theology.
Hayek referred to St. Augustine’s dialogues as the starting point for the concept of order.

In these discussions, Augustine notes that the extraordinary complexity of the universe is literally incomprehensible by any one individual. He describes not only the inevitable sense of powerlessness that humans feel in the face of this larger order but also the distortions that come from our individual and subjective perspective. “The situation,” he wrote, “is akin to that of one who, confined to surveying a single section of a mosaic floor, looked at it too closely and then blamed the artisan for being ignorant of order and composition.” The apparent disorder of the part is actually an artifact of the limited perspective of the viewer, who “failed to notice the larger mosaic world” that “comes together into the unity of a beautiful portrait.” The individual striving for a more synoptic perspective always runs the risk of misidentifying disorder for its opposite—and vice versa. He wrote that “unable to grasp the harmony and interaction of the universe as a whole, and hurt by what is beyond their ken, such people rashly conclude that things are inherently ugly and disorderly.”

zh: 奥古斯丁提示了一种有违直觉的观察方式。观者必须避免把眼前的局部误当作整体的面貌。这里蕴含着一种对反向观察之可能性的召唤：看似秩序者实则可能是无序；看似无序者实则可能是秩序。批评社会主义看不见更大的秩序，乃是新自由主义常见的批判。正如弗朗茨·伯姆（Franz Böhm）在一篇论“秩序的理念”的文章中所说，社会主义思想家“在竞争经济中根本拒绝看见任何秩序，只看见无政府状态与混沌，并否认其中存在任何规律，除了弱肉强食的丛林法则”。
我的叙述已经表明，日内瓦学派的新自由主义与其说是市场理论或经济学理论，不如说是关于法律与国家的理论。秩序全球主义可以被视为一种否定神学，它宣称世界经济崇高玄远、不可言说。
en: Augustine suggests a counterintuitive mode of observation. The viewer must guard against being deceived by a part misrepresenting the whole. There is a call here for the potential of inverse observation: that which appears as order may in fact be disorder; and that which appears as disorder may in fact be order. It was a common neoliberal critique of socialism that they failed to see the greater order. As Franz Böhm put it in an article on “the idea of Ordo,” socialist thinkers “refused to catch sight of an order at all in the competitive economy, only saw anarchy and chaos, and denied the existence of any laws in it except the law of the jungle.”

My narrative has shown that Geneva School neoliberalism is less a theory of the market or of economics than of law and the state. Ordoglobalism can be thought of as a negative theology, contending that the world economy is sublime and ineffable.

zh: 日内瓦学派的新自由主义者有时被人指摘犯了经济主义——即把经济看作一部自主运转、能够产出某些预期结果的机器；但他们其实视经济为宇宙性的存在：它被围封在法律与政治制度之中，始终处于一个开放未定的生成过程。哈耶克对宏观经济学使用数学以“给政治家留下印象……这大概是职业经济学家所做的事中最接近施展魔术的一件”嗤之以鼻。
他说自己始终觉得本应写一部针对米尔顿·弗里德曼《实证经济学论文集》（Essays in Positive Economics）的批判，因为它“与凯恩斯的那一部一样危险”。
与芝加哥学派不同，日内瓦学派反对经济学的数学化，从而也就堵死了对经济作广泛预测和建模的可能性。它既不取理性预期，也不取完全竞争，并认为宣称能够判定“效率”或“最优”结果，既是堂吉诃德式的妄想，又是狂妄的僭越。近年来，彼得斯曼甚至把2008年金融危机的罪责归于芝加哥学派的“有效市场假说”——该假说认为“市场价格反映了所有相关信息”。
以彼得斯曼本人把世贸组织倡导为一部“世界经济宪法”为表征，我所称的日内瓦学派把奥地利学派对知识限度与全球尺度的强调，同德国秩序自由主义对制度与政治决断时刻的强调结合在了一起。
en: Rather than the economism of which they are sometimes accused— in the sense of seeing the economy as machine-like, autonomous, and capable of producing certain desired outcomes—Geneva School neoliberals saw the economy as cosmic, encased in legal and political institutions, and always in an open-ended process of becoming. Hayek scoffed at the use of mathematics in macroeconomics to “impress politicians . . . which is the nearest thing to the practice of magic that occurs among professional economists.”
He said that he always felt he should have written a critique of Milton Friedman’s
“every bit as dangerous as that of Keynes.”

Unlike the Chicago School, the Geneva School opposed the mathematization of economics and thus foreclosed the possibility of extensive forecasting and modeling of the economy. It rejected both rational expectations and perfect competition and held the claim of determining “efficiency” or “optimal” outcomes to be both quixotic and hubristic. In recent years Petersmann has even laid the blame for the financial crisis of 2008 at the feet of the “efficient markets hypothesis” of the Chicago School that “market prices reflect all relevant information.”

As represented by Petersmann’s own advocacy for the WTO as a “worldwide economic constitution,” what I call the Geneva School combined the Austrian emphasis on the limits of knowledge and the global scale with the German ordoliberal emphasis on institutions and the moment of the political decision.

zh: 否认“经济”本身的存在或可见性，其用意正是使社会正义、平等或再分配的规划变得不可想象。但它并不使权力消失。人们时常声称，新自由主义者最主要的障眼法是把国家藏起来，但即便对主要理论家作浮光掠影的阅读也会发现，关于国家的积极构想俯拾皆是。日内瓦学派新自由主义者真正遮掩的东西并非国家，而是权力的不对称。的确，诉诸复杂性与不可知性是一种有用的治理实践。全球金融危机之后，德国财政部长沃尔夫冈·朔伊布勒（Wolfgang Schäuble）说：“我们从弗里德里希·奥古斯特·冯·哈耶克那里学到……社会与经济不是机器。任何人若相信能够获得全面知识从而掌控事态，他拥有的并非知识，而只是知识的僭妄。”
学者们指出，与我们当今知识社会的观念相反，宣称无知与不可知才最有助于为那些被认定应对全球系统性风险负责的人开脱——例如在金融世界里便是如此。
en: To disavow the existence or visibility of “economies” themselves intentionally makes projects of social justice, equality, or redistribution unthinkable. But it does not make power disappear. It is sometimes claimed that the main sleight of hand for neoliberals is to hide the state, but even a cursory reading of the main theorists shows that a positive vision for the state is everywhere. The main thing the Geneva School neoliberals hide is not the state but asymmetries of power. Indeed, the invocation of complexity and unknowability is a useful practice of government. After the global financial crisis, German finance minister Wolfgang Schäuble said, “We have learned from Friedrich August von Hayek … that society and the economy are not machines. Anyone who believes it is possible to acquire comprehensive knowledge enabling him to control events has no knowledge, but only a pretense of knowledge.”

Contrary to the notion of our present-day knowledge society, scholars have noted, it is professions of ignorance and unknowability that are most helpful in exonerating those putatively responsible for global systemic risk, as, for example, in the world of finance.

zh: 不了解整体，却通晓维持整体所必需的规则——这就是本书所描述的日内瓦学派一脉新自由主义的精髓。朔伊布勒此后在欧元区危机中的行径表明，承认经济的不可知，并不意味着愿意秉持务实的开放心态，或通过多元群体之间的谈判与妥协达成新的治理策略。恰恰相反，它意味着一种遇事愈发一概诉诸原则和规则的倾向。接受经济为政府的一道内在限制，意味着毫不通融地恪守那些被视为围封不可知的经济本身所必需的法律。
en: Not knowing the totality while knowing the rules needed to maintain it is the essence of the Geneva School variety of neoliberalism described in this book. As the example of Schäuble’s subsequent conduct in the Eurozone crisis showed, conceding the unknowability of the economy does not mean a willingness to exercise pragmatic open-mindedness or arrive at new management strategies through negotiation and compromise among diverse constituencies. Instead it meant an even more rigid tendency to default to the principle and the rule. Accepting the economy as an internal limit to government means inflexible adherence to the laws seen as necessary to encase the unknowable economy itself.

zh: 回望这一个世纪，人们会注意到：正是在出现对经济实行全面监督之尝试的节点上，新自由主义者的动员最为直接。最突出的有两次，分别在1930年代与1970年代——两次都处于帝国终结的当口。1930年代，新自由主义者动员起来，反对国家层面的计划，反对那种认为无须协调一致的全球框架便可看清并驾驭经济的信念。1970年代，他们抨击那些借助计算机的改革主义者——这些人企图把世界经济当作一个整体来透视。学者们指出个中的讽刺：恰恰就在世界上占多数的非白人人口通过非殖民化主张法律平等的同一时刻，有影响力的社会科学诸流派却得出了个人并不存在的结论。
我们在本书中看到过相似的情形：在自主性得以主张的时刻，新自由主义者的回应是申扬个人主义——但更要紧的是，申扬体系性的相互依存；这种相互依存关系使得一国或一个区域无法按照有悖于资本与货物自由流动要求的逻辑行事。
en: Looking back at the century, one notes that it was at points when there was an attempt at comprehensive oversight over the economy that neoliberals mobilized most directly. The two most prominent were in the 1930s and 1970s—both moments at the end of empire. In the 1930s neoliberals mobilized against planning at the national level and the belief that the economy could be seen and directed without a harmonized global framework. In the 1970s they criticized computer-aided reformists who sought to see the world economy as a whole. Scholars have pointed out the irony that it was at the exact moment that the world’s majority of nonwhite people claimed legal equality through decolonization that influential branches of social science concluded that the individual did not exist.

We have seen something similar here: at the moment of the assertion of autonomy, the response of neoliberals was to assert individualism—but even more so, systemic interdependence that negated the possibility of national or regional action with a logic inconsistent with the dictates of free movement of capital and goods.

zh: 在新自由主义的世界秩序构想中，世界经济通过以下方式对各个国家施行纪律：持续存在的危机威胁，投资外逃对社会政策扩张的惩罚，以及针对政府支出增加而发动的货币投机攻击。国家之间对公民的争夺，仍是其长盛不衰的愿景。我的叙述表明，那个以解放市场为宣言的规划同时也是一项制度设计。正如彼得斯曼所言：“规则不会自动执行。”
哈耶克式对设计的否认，并没有把他的种种主张变成别的东西——它们恰恰就是设计。即便把世界经济理解为信息处理器与自组织系统，它仍需要干预来校准规则。勒普克1942年提出的要求历久不衰：“如果我们想要一个自由市场，那么条件、规则与制度的框架就必须愈加强硬、愈加不容通融。自由放任——可以，但必须在一个由常设的、目光敏锐的市场警察所设定的框架之内——取这个词最广泛的含义。”
新自由主义运动一个重要流派的道德力量，正来自这样一种承诺：通过辨识——乃至创造——一套适用于全球的市场监管力量，来保护全球贸易体系那复杂的、甚至不可知的相互依存。
en: In the neoliberal vision of world order, the world economy exercises discipline on individual nations through the perpetual threat of crisis, the flight of investment that punishes expansion in social policy, and speculative attacks on currencies in reaction to increases in government spending. The competition for citizens between states remains a lasting vision. What my narrative has shown is that the declared project of liberating the market was also one of institutional design. As Petersmann put it, “Rules do not enforce themselves.”

The Hayekian disavowal of design does not transform his proposals into anything other than precisely that. Even understood as an information processor and a self-organizing system, the world economy requires intervention to calibrate the rules. Röpke’s demand from 1942 is an enduring one: “If we desire a free market, the framework of conditions, rules and institutions must be all the stronger and more inflexible. Laissez-faire—yes, but within a framework laid down by a permanent and clear-sighted market police in the widest sense of this word.”

The moral force for an important school of the neoliberal movement came from the commitment to protect the complex and even unknowable interdependence of the global trading system through the identification of—even creation of—a market police cut to the dimensions of the world.

zh: 日内瓦学派新自由主义的精髓可以概括为若干要点。它们不是律令，而是命题。尽管细究起来可以指出种种分歧，它们概括了本书所关注的知识分子之间的基本共识：
en: The essence of Geneva School neoliberalism can be summarized in a series of points. These are meant not as commandments but as propositions. Although one could split hairs by pointing to variations, they offer a basic consensus shared by the intellectuals at the core of this book:

zh: 1. 没有完美的市场，因为没有完美的知识。经济的崇高地位意味着，能成为人类设计对象的只是规则的一“薄层”。
en: 1. There is no perfect market because no knowledge is perfect. The sublime status of the economy means that only a “thin layer” of rules can be the objects of human design.

zh: 2. 全球主义高于民族主义。唯有资本主义是国际主义的；社会主义则永远是民族主义的。
en: 2. Globalism trumps nationalism. Only capitalism is internationalist; socialism is always nationalist.

zh: 3. 世界经济秩序有赖于保护所有权（dominium，即财产的统治），使之不受统治权（imperium，即国家的统治）的越权侵犯。
en: 3. World economic order depends on the protection of dominium (the rule of property) against the overreach of imperium (the rule of states).

zh: 4. 消费者主权高于国家主权。公／私之分比外／内之分更为重要。
en: 4. Consumer sovereignty trumps national sovereignty. The public / private distinction is more important than the foreign / domestic.

zh: 5. 世界法高于世界国家。国际机构应当充当保护并推进竞争的机制，而不为大众提出权利主张提供空间。
en: 5. World law trumps a world state. International institutions should act as mechanisms for protecting and furthering competition without offering spaces for popular claims-making.

zh: 6. 民主对市场秩序的正常运转构成潜在威胁。因此，必须设置防范民主之破坏力的保障措施。
en: 6. Democracy is a potential threat to the functioning of the market order. Therefore, safeguards against the disruptive capacity of democracy are necessary.

zh: 7. 民主的危险在于它为再分配的要求提供了正当性。一切世界经济问题都植根于国内的分配斗争。
en: 7. Democracy’s danger is its legitimation of demands for redistribution. All world economic problems are rooted in domestic distribution struggles.

zh: 8. 法律是逐步演化形成的，而非人为制定的。法官与学者的裁判优于议会创制的立法。
en: 8. Laws are grown, not made. Adjudication by judges and scholars is preferable to legislation created by parliaments.

zh: 9. 同法（isonomy，相同的法律）高于自治（autonomy，自己的法律）。人天性遵循规则。因此，从习惯中形成的规则必须由成文规制加以保护。
en: 9. Isonomy (same law) trumps autonomy (own law). Humans follow rules by nature. Therefore, rules-as-regularities must be protected by rules-as-regulation.

zh: 10. 法律必须确保可预期性，以引导人类的未来行动。具体而言，它必须保护价格在传递有关未来的知识方面所扮演的角色。
en: 10. Law must ensure predictability as a guide to future human action. Specifically, it must protect the role of prices in transmitting knowledge about the future.

zh: 11. 规则为人类行动的全球反馈机制创造条件，为市场的自发秩序搭建框架。
en: 11. Rules create the conditions for global feedback mechanisms of human action and the framework for the spontaneous order of the market.

zh: 12. 人类对知识作出回应，其中许多知识并未进入人的意识。这种知识的核心是禁令——那条说“不”的规则。因此，国际机构的作用主要是施加限制。
en: 12. Humans respond to knowledge, much of it unconscious. Central to that knowledge is the prohibition, the rule that says no. Thus, the role of international institutions is primarily negative.

zh: 13. 一体化同样主要是消极的，致力于消除各领土之间的壁垒。然而，消极一体化这一规划本身就是一种积极主动、持续不断的事业。它需要制度来保证这一过程顺畅运转。
en: 13. Integration is also primarily negative, devoted to the removal of barriers between territories. Yet the project of negative integration is itself an active and ongoing undertaking. Institutions are required to keep this process functioning smoothly.

zh: 14. 须以法典保障跨境贸易，而跨境贸易是整体秩序得以形成的必要条件。
en: 14. Trade over borders must be enshrined in legal code and is required for the coalescence of the overall order.

zh: 15. 一体化不是创造新事物，而是恢复失落之物。
en: 15. Integration is not the creation of something new but the restoration of something lost.

zh: 本书沿全球北方与全球南方的断层带，透过日内瓦学派的谱系，讲述了新自由主义的兴起；对于帝国的终结，该学派开出的解方是为世界经济颁布一部统一的法律。1984年，暮年的哈耶克回顾朝圣山学社的创立时，并没有使用布什授予他自由勋章时那种言必称先见之明的高调语言。相反，他说自己1947年的目标是“组建一个国际协会”，讨论“宪法对政府的约束问题”。
在他屡屡回到的那个比喻里，目标是通过治理与法律的框架，把民主的后殖民国家像尤利西斯那样绑在世界经济的桅杆上。
en: This book has told the story of the emergence of neoliberalism along the fault line of Global North and Global South through the genealogy of the Geneva School, whose solution to the end of empire was to promulgate one law for the world economy. Reflecting back as an elderly man in 1984 on the founding of the MPS, Hayek did not use the high-flown language of foresight that Bush would in granting him the Medal of Freedom. Instead he said that his goal in 1947 had been “to form an international association” to discuss “the problems of constitutional constraints on government.”
In the metaphor to which he frequently returned, the goal was to tie the Ulysses of the democratic postcolonial state to the mast of the world economy through frameworks of government and law.

zh: 西雅图与自下而上的解决方案

children: SEATTLE AND THE FIX FROM BELOW

zh: 莫大的讽刺在于：秩序全球主义几乎恰恰在其取得最重大胜利的时刻陷入了危机。关贸总协定变身世贸组织，是日内瓦学派在二十世纪的巅峰时刻。此话不虚——尽管这一机构的创设，靠的并非他们高明的智识远见或政治说服之力，而是世界头号强国美国的直接经济利益。制造业这一传统优势部门面临新兴经济体的竞争，加之担心美国在娱乐、医药与软件方面的优势会被盗版与模仿蚕食殆尽——凡此促使美国连哄带压、恐吓威逼，让世界各国同意了一项明显偏袒霸权国的安排。
然而，无论世贸组织得以成立的条件是什么，日内瓦学派的新自由主义者都有理由庆贺：其架构的种种细节打上了他们的印记。正如本书所勾勒的那样，世贸组织之下的世界贸易体制，把治理欧洲的种种规则与制度放大到了全球尺度。
en: It is a great irony that ordoglobalism entered a crisis at nearly the precise moment of its most significant victory. The transformation of the GATT into the WTO was the crowning moment in the twentieth century for the Geneva School. This was true despite the fact that the creation of the institution was the outcome, not of their superior intellectual vision or powers of political persuasion, but of the brute economic interests of the world’s leading power, the United States. Competition from emerging economies in its traditionally strong sectors of manufacturing, and a fear that the U.S. advantage in entertainment, pharmaceuticals, and software would be bootlegged and imitated away, led the United States to cajole, pressure, and intimidate the world’s countries to agree to an arrangement that clearly favored the hegemon.

Yet whatever the conditions were for the realization of the WTO, Geneva School neoliberals could rightly celebrate having put their stamp on the details of its structure. In the ways outlined in these pages, the world trading system under the WTO scaled up the rules and institutions governing Europe to the global scale.

zh: 在123个国家签署建立世贸组织的协定前六个月，该组织未来的总干事彼得·萨瑟兰（Peter Sutherland）在伦敦经济事务研究所（Institute of Economic Affairs）发表第三届哈耶克纪念讲座时，为上述说法提供了佐证。他说，世贸组织的起草者“汲取了哈耶克的两个关键洞见——价格体系在传递信息方面的作用，以及法治的重要性”。
萨瑟兰是哈耶克思想再完美不过的代言人。他是一位律师出身的爱尔兰人，1984年至1988年出任欧洲竞争事务专员，因为他看到竞争法是推动欧洲走向联邦式一体化所能用到的最有力工具。他的积极行动为他赢得了雅克·德洛尔（Jacques Delors）赐的外号“警长”，因为他雷厉风行地运用竞争法推动欧共体内部贸易自由化，并把一个个国家拉到欧洲法院面前。
有学者称他是“欧盟委员会中新自由主义理念的化身”，因为他借助欧洲法院终结了政府对本国产业的资助，并强力提升竞争。
en: Six months before 123 nations signed the agreement to create the WTO, its future director, Peter Sutherland, gave credence to this claim when he delivered the Third Hayek Memorial Lecture at the Institute of Economic Affairs in London. The drafters of the WTO, he said, “drew on two of Hayek’s key insights—the role of the price system in conveying information and the importance of the rule of law.”

Sutherland was the perfect spokesperson for the Hayekian message. An Irishman trained as a lawyer, he took the position as European competition commissioner from 1984 to 1988 because he saw that competition law was the most powerful tool available for federal European integration. His activism earned him the nickname “the sheriff” from Jacques Delors, because he used competition law aggressively to liberalize trade within the European Community and bring individual nations to the European Court of Justice.
One scholar calls him the “embodiment of neoliberal ideas in the European Commission” as he used the European Court of Justice to end state funding of national industries and ramp up competition.

zh: 哈耶克关于法治的规范性构想包含三项要素：强制执行的机制、司法审查与同法（isonomy）。萨瑟兰可以指出：上诉机构便是执行的机制；世贸组织协定以知识产权条款保障私人贸易权利；一切国家——包括全球南方各国——都被置于贸易纪律的管辖之下，由此生成了同法。萨瑟兰对价格体系的援引，与哈耶克的信念一脉相通——后者把世界经济看作一个巨大的知识库，必须借助价格信号才能利用其中的信息。哈耶克为自由贸易与资本自由流动所作的辩护，要害正在于调用世界居民的知识。正如哈耶克在其1979年三部曲结尾所说：“如果我们想利用栖居于这个世界不同位置的个体所掌握的那些有别的事实性知识，就必须让市场以不针对任何个人的信号告诉他们，如何运用这些知识，既最符合他们自己的利益，也最符合普遍的利益。”
世贸组织背后的哲学，反映了哈耶克式的信念：该组织是控制论式法律秩序的守护者，确保价格信号在层层嵌套的规制空间中畅通无阻地传输。
en: Hayek’s normative vision of the rule of law contained the features of a means of enforcement, judicial review, and isonomy. Sutherland could point to the Appellate Body as a mechanism of enforcement, the individual trading rights protected for intellectual property under the terms of the WTO Agreement, and the isonomy produced by the subjection of all nations—including those of the Global South—to trade disciplines. Sutherland’s invocation of the price system connected to Hayek’s belief in the world economy as a giant depository of knowledge to be accessed through the information of price signals. Hayek’s argument for free trade and free movement of capital was about tapping the knowledge of the world’s inhabitants. As Hayek put it at the end of his 1979 trilogy: “If we are to make use of the distinct factual knowledge of the individuals inhabiting different locations on this world, we must allow them to be told by the impersonal signals of the market how they had best use them in their own as well as in the general interest.”

The philosophy behind the WTO reflected a Hayekian belief in the organization as the guardian of the cybernetic legal order, ensuring unimpeded transmission of price signals across the strata of nested spaces of regulation.

zh: 从这个角度看，世贸组织像是一场凯旋：它提供法治，校准价格机制的线路，让信息的接收愈发精准。然而，哈耶克在颂扬价格信息的同时，也承认知识是危险的，它可能危及体系本身。正如他在《自由秩序原理》中所言，正是“对各种可能性的认识”在全球的扩散，要求发起一场反向运动，以锁定竞争政策与永续的调适。哈耶克自1930年代以来便讲得很明白：全球资本主义的两个必需条件，是世界经济的不可见性与匿名性。世贸组织却违背了这些规矩。事实上，它开始运作仅仅四年，有关该组织的知识之扩散便酿成了一场自下而上促成的停摆。
en: From this perspective the WTO looked like a triumph, offering the rule of law and calibrating the circuitry of the price mechanism to allow for ever more precise reception of information. Yet even as Hayek praised information of prices, he also conceded that knowledge was dangerous. It could imperil the system. As he put it in

it was the global spread of the “knowledge of possibilities” that required a countermovement to lock in policies of competition and perpetual adjustment. Hayek had made clear since the 1930s that two necessities for global capitalism were the invisibility and the anonymity of the world economy. The WTO transgressed those rules. Indeed, just four years after it began its work, it was the spread of knowledge
the organization led to a shutdown engineered from below.

zh: 1999年，大规模抗议导致世贸组织西雅图会议流产。在以扬·图姆利尔命名的讲座系列中，萨瑟兰称西雅图是“该机构的分水岭”，它造成了“世贸体系在有效政治支持上的根本亏空”。他说：“西雅图造就了一代人、一支大军般的世贸组织憎恨者——而他们手里有选票。”
马丁·沃尔夫（Martin Wolf）在同一讲座系列中指出：“决策者改变了贸易体系的规模、经济覆盖范围和影响，也改变了它的法律效力，与此同时，也提高了它的政治能见度。昔日它不过是一小撮博学精干的决策者与技术官僚的玩物，如今却成了五花八门的非政府组织激烈施压的焦点。”随着人们声称“现行的政府间安排是‘不民主的’”，“多数决”这个老对手又回来了。
en: In 1999, massive protests led to the cancellation of the meeting of the WTO in Seattle. In a lecture series devoted to Jan Tumlir, Sutherland called Seattle a “watershed for the institution” that created “a fundamental deficit in effective political support for the WTO system.” “Seattle created a generation and a legion of WTO-haters,” he said, “and they have votes.”

Martin Wolf noted in the same lecture series, “As decision-makers transformed the size, economic scope, impact and legal potency of the trading system, they also increased its political visibility. What had previously been the play thing of a limited group of highly knowledgeable policy-makers and technocrats has become the focus of fierce pressure from a wide range of non-governmental organisations.” The old foe of “majoritarianism” returned as people claimed “that the present inter-governmental arrangement is ‘undemocratic.’ ”

zh: 学者们只在后来——有些人不无懊悔地——意识到：全球经济治理也许在能够按情势展开幕后谈判、保留多种退出选项时运作得最好，而法律化可能妨碍它。

在全球尺度上把规则保持一致，是一项注定庞大的工程，公众不可能不加注意。而一旦注意起来，他们便要问：为什么如此多的决策以他们的名义做出，却几乎没有他们的参与。恰恰是去政治化国际经济关系的努力，最终需要一个高度可见的项目，而这个项目不可能不把自己变成政治争议的靶子。这正是新自由主义的制度解决方案的核心难题之一，而梅斯特马克是少数看清此点的人之一。正是借助施密特，他洞察到去政治化必然是政治性的，也没有轻信那个在经验上可以被证伪的念头——仿佛只要把某些事务交给“法治”，就能把它们永久抬升到民众抗争可能性之上。为了维护世界经济宪法守护者这一理念而否认世贸组织内部政治的可能性，实际上并未放逐政治，它只是在西雅图抗议一类的行动果然爆发时拿不出任何参照框架罢了。看来，即使——尤其——不给人姓名牌或话筒，人们也要发出自己的声音。
en: Scholars realized only later, some ruefully, that global economic governance may have worked best when it was performed in an ad hoc, backroom manner, through negotiation, with many exit options, rather than through legalization.

Making the rules consistent at a global scale was such a necessarily large undertaking that the public could not help but notice. When they did, they asked why so many decisions were being made in their name with so little of their input. The very attempt to depoliticize international economic relations ended up requiring a highly visible project that could not help but make itself the object of political controversy. This was one of the core problems of the neoliberal fix that Mestmäcker was one of the few to see clearly. It was by appealing to Schmitt that he perceived the necessarily political nature of depoliticization and did not fall for the empirically falsifiable idea that simply relegating certain matters to the “rule of law” would somehow raise them permanently above the possibility of popular contestation. To deny the possibility of politics in the WTO in the interest of a notion of the guardians of the constitution of the world economy did not actually banish politics, it merely offered no frame of reference when actions like the Seattle protests did erupt. People will use their voice, it seemed, even—or especially—if no nameplate or microphone is provided.

zh: 一些学者认为，世贸组织以及围封全球市场的其他努力所面临的最持久挑战，是世界经济缺少一个demos（人民）。
然而，到世界经济之中去寻找一个demos，便是把问题提错了；这也犯了一种范畴错误。正如我的叙述所示，自由主义者以及后来的新自由主义者在整个二十世纪里，都把世界经济的空间设想为一个与代议制政府的空间相分离的空间。新自由主义的制度解决方案的种种变体，其设计精神与其说是“撤销人民”（undoing the demos）本身，不如说是把人民隔离起来、拴住，圈进划定的区域。
如果说世界经济没有一个demos，这恰恰正是其要义所在。那是一个只有众人而无人民的世界。
en: Some scholars argue that the most enduring challenge for the WTO and other efforts at encasing global markets has been the absence of a demos for the world economy.

Yet to look for a demos in the world economy is to pose the question wrong. It is also to commit a category error. As my narrative has shown, liberals and later neoliberals thought of the space of the world economy through the twentieth century as being a space separate from that of representative government. The many variations of the neoliberal fix were designed in the spirit, not of “undoing the demos” per se, but of sequestering and leashing it, penning it into prescribed areas.
If the world economy did not have a demos, this was precisely the point. It was a world of people but a world without a people.

zh: 西雅图之后，急于重塑机构形象的总干事迈克·穆尔（Mike Moore）宣称：“我们得让这该死的事重新运转起来……我们得重新打造品牌！”
其后的那一轮贸易谈判至今未能完成，却被冠以“多哈发展回合”之名——参与者后来承认，这分明是一桩明目张胆的公关之举。2005年，帕斯卡尔·拉米（Pascal Lamy）在后来获胜的世贸组织总干事竞选中，首次使用“日内瓦共识”（the Geneva Consensus）一词，为这套新品牌命了名。
他的底气来自其担任欧盟贸易委员的经验；本着秩序全球主义的精神，他声称“欧洲的建设事实上是人类迄今尝试过的最雄心勃勃的超国家治理实验”，而“作为一个实验室”，“欧洲经验……为全球层面提供了有趣的进路”。
拉米宣称，日内瓦共识——与他据称取而代之的华盛顿共识相对——将致力于“使全球化更具人性，并建立进一步的正义与公平”。
国际货币基金组织一边开始对减贫表示口头重视，一边继续紧盯削减公共预算这些老议题；世贸组织如法炮制，试图增添一套新辞令，却不改变机构的基本结构。
en: Eager to reframe the institution after Seattle, the director-general Mike Moore declared, “We’ve got to get this fuckin’ show back on the road. … We’ve got to rebrand!”

The subsequent trade round, still not completed, was dubbed the “Doha Development Round” in what participants later conceded was a blatant act of public relations. The new brand was given another name when Pascal Lamy used the term “the Geneva Consensus” for the first time in 2005 during his successful campaign for director general of the WTO.

He was working from his experience as the EU trade commissioner and, true to the spirit of ordoglobalism, contended that “the building of Europe is in fact the most ambitious experiment in supranational governance ever attempted” and that, as “a laboratory,” “the European experience … offers interesting avenues for the global level.”
Lamy claimed that the Geneva Consensus, against the Washington Consensus that it putatively replaced, would be dedicated to “humanizing globalization and establishing further justice and equity.”

Like the IMF, which began to pay lip service to poverty reduction while continuing to focus on the old key issues of cutting public budgets, the WTO sought to add new rhetoric without changing the basic structure of the organization.

zh: 西雅图是秩序全球主义的一场生存危机。它把崇高的世界经济拉回了地面。民众对围封市场的拒绝，这一前景对新自由主义思想而言始终是个难题。许多批评者指出，转向威权解决方案的诱惑似乎总是近在眼前，哈耶克与弗里德曼造访奥古斯托·皮诺切特（Augusto Pinochet）的智利便是最明显的例证。谈及皮诺切特，哈耶克说他“宁愿要一个自由主义的独裁者，也不要一个缺乏自由主义的民主政府”，并说“一个独裁者按自由主义原则施政是可能的”——同时附加说，这只能是一种“临时的过渡性安排”。
哈耶克的表态，让人想起勒普克1940年关于“独裁式民主”的讨论，也让人想起米塞斯1927年的论断：意大利“法西斯主义以及旨在建立独裁政权的类似运动，出于最好的意图，它们的干预暂时挽救了欧洲文明。法西斯主义由此为自身赢下的功德，将在历史上永世长存”。
循着两害相权取其轻的逻辑，压制来自左翼的破坏性力量，不时使一部分新自由主义者认为支持独裁者未尝不可。米塞斯1922年写道：“我们整个文明有赖于这样一个事实：人总是成功击退了再分配者的进攻。”
en: Seattle was an existential crisis for ordoglobalism. It brought the sublime world economy down to earth. The prospect of a popular rejection of the encasement of markets has always posed a problem for neoliberal thought. Many critics have noted that the turn to an authoritarian solution always seems close at hand, with Hayek and Friedman’s visits to Augusto Pinochet’s Chile being exhibit A. Referring to Pinochet, Hayek said he would “prefer a liberal dictator to a democratic government lacking liberalism” and that “it is possible for a dictator to govern in a liberal way”—while qualifying that this should be only a “temporary transitional arrangement.”

Hayek’s statements recalled both Röpke’s discussion of “dictatorial democracy” in 1940 and Mises’s point in 1927 that Italian “fascism and similar movements aiming at the establishment of dictatorships are full of the best intentions and that their intervention has, for the moment, saved European civilization. The merit that Fascism has thereby won for itself will live on eternally in history.”

Following the logic of the lesser evil, the suppression of a disruptive force from the left periodically made support for dictators thinkable for some neoliberals. Mises wrote in 1922, “Our whole civilization rests on the fact that men have always succeeded in beating off the attack of the re-distributors.”

zh: 在世贸组织遭到抗议冲击之后，日内瓦学派的领军人物既未在其理论中采纳皮诺切特选项，也未求助于“自由主义独裁者”，而是转向了皮诺切特最有力的反对者们的语言——人权的话语。日内瓦学派新自由主义者的回应是挪用与重新定义。回响着菲利普·科特尼战后关于将资本转移海外的权利应被视为一项人权的呼声，他们加倍倚重哈耶克曾经鄙薄的同一套人权话语，来支撑自己的规划。本书已经表明：把贸易权利、市场权利与资本权利改铸为个人权利，是由国际商会（ICC）与新自由主义者在1945年前后针对联合国的经济社会权利理念提出的；在1950至1960年代，这种主张以市场自由和市场公民身份的形式纳入了欧洲一体化进程；在1970至1980年代关贸总协定改革的过程中，它又被放大到世贸组织。西雅图之后，恩斯特-乌尔里希·彼得斯曼（Ernst-Ulrich Petersmann）成为又一场以人权为核心的自由主义改造最显眼、最高调的代言人。借助喷涌而出的著述，他鼓吹一种由分层制度构成、保护个人贸易与移动资本之权利的规范性世界经济秩序。新自由主义联邦主义的规划被推至公众眼前，进而被重新想象为一项保护普遍人权的事业。
en: The leading thinkers of the Geneva School after the assault on the WTO took neither the Pinochet option nor the recourse to a “liberal dictator” in their theorizing. Rather, they turned to the language of Pinochet’s most effective opponents: that of human rights. The response of Geneva School neoliberals was one of co-optation and redefinition. With echoes of Philip Cortney’s postwar calls for the human right of capital flight, they doubled down on the very language of human rights scorned by Hayek to buttress their project. This book has shown that the recasting of trading rights, market rights, and capital rights as indi

rights was proposed by the International Chamber of Commerce (ICC) and neoliberals against the United Nations’ idea of social and economic rights around 1945, incorporated as the market freedoms and market citizens of the European integration project in the 1950s and 1960s, and scaled up to the WTO in the course of GATT reform in the 1970s and 1980s. After Seattle, Ernst-Ulrich Petersmann became the most visible and vocal spokesperson for yet another renovation of liberalism with human rights at its core. In a flood of publications, he propagated the idea of a normative world economic order built of stratified institutions protecting the indi
right to trade and move capital. Thrust into the public eye, the project of neoliberal federalism was reimagined as one of protecting universal human rights.

zh: 颇堪玩味的讽刺是，彼得斯曼曾批评全球南方的七十七国集团（G-77）所使用的权利话语，只有当权利被重新定义为资本与货物的自由流动时他才提倡权利，尤其是在欧洲一体化的语境中。他在西雅图之后的论调也发生了同样工具性的转变。抗议爆发前他发表的最后一篇文章——部分基于他为香港政府提供的咨询——核心词是“竞争”。他三次援引哈耶克，谴责欠发达国家缺少竞争法，并呼吁“在世贸组织内部开展‘竞争倡导’……在世贸组织推动‘竞争与创业文化’”。
他在西雅图之后发表的第一篇文章框架迥异，题为《是时候将人权纳入世贸组织法律的主流了》。
他以日内瓦高等国际问题研究院（Graduate Institute of International Studies）教授的身份写道：“世贸组织西雅图部长级会议的失败，以及暴力抗议者针对基于世贸组织规则的世界贸易掀起的‘西雅图茶党’，被描述为一记‘警钟’，提醒贸易外交官们需要更具说服力地向国内公民解释世贸组织规则的正当性与‘人权功能’。”
这一表态发表在《国际经济法杂志》（Journal of International Economic Law）上——该刊1998年趁世贸组织看似凯旋之际创刊。在该刊第一期上，彼得斯曼曾盛赞世贸组织的“宪政功能”——推进“国际法治”，其中居于核心的是“私人知识产权……作为基本的个人权利”。
仅仅两年之后，他便把西雅图形容为“警钟”，可见这对日内瓦学派想象力的挑战何等严重。
en: It is a revealing irony that Petersmann was a critic of the language of rights in the hands of the Global South in the G-77 and advocated rights only when redefined as free movement of capital and goods, especially in the context of European integration. One can track a similarly instrumental change in his tone after Seattle. In the last article he published before the protests—based in part on his consulting for the government of Hong Kong—Petersmann’s key term was “competition.” Citing Hayek three times, he denounced the absence of competition laws in less developed countries and called for “ ‘competition advocacy’ within the WTO … and promoting a ‘competition and entrepreneurship culture’ in the WTO.”
His first article after Seattle was framed very differently. It was titled “Time for Mainstreaming Human Rights into WTO Law.”

Writing as a professor at the Graduate Institute of International Studies in Geneva, he wrote that the “failure of the WTO’s ministerial conference at Seattle and the ‘Seattle Tea Party’ by violent protesters against world trade based on WTO rules, have been described as a ‘wake up call’ for trade diplomats who need to explain more convincingly the legitimacy and ‘human rights functions’ of WTO rules to domestic citizens.”
This statement was presented in the Journal of Inter

a publication launched in 1998 in the wake of the apparent victory of the WTO. In the journal’s first issue, Petersmann had praised the “constitutional functions” of the WTO in promoting the “international rule of law,” including centrally “private intellectual property rights … as basic individual rights.”
His description of Seattle as a “wake up call” just two years later suggests the seriousness of the challenge to the Geneva School imagination.

zh: 西雅图之后，彼得斯曼的著述中出现了一个此前几乎完全不见的词：“正当性”。他直接回应抗议，说“在如今国际货币基金组织、世界银行与世贸组织部长级会议期间如今经常出现的街头示威中，公民们正在提醒各国政府：需要使以国家为中心的传统国际法与国际组织适应他们的人权，适应那正在兴起的‘民主权’”。
他实际上认同抗议者，却继而以一种非常特定的方式解读他们的人权话语。他辩称，真正可耻的丑闻在于，联合国人权公约“对经济自由、财产权与法治不提供任何有效保护”。
他一方面寻求为世贸组织奠定人权语言的基础，另一方面又寻求把经济语言插入居支配地位的人权话语。“世贸组织法律对人权的传统漠视，正变得如同国际人权文书对经济自由与贸易自由——作为个人福祉之前提——的顽固漠视一样过时。”
en: After Seattle, a term appeared in Petersmann’s writings that was previously almost entirely absent: “legitimacy.” He responded directly to the protest, saying that “in the now regular street demonstrations at the ministerial conferences of the IMF, the World Bank and WTO, citizens are reminding governments of the need to adjust the state-centered traditional international law and international organizations to their human rights and to the emerging ‘right to democracy.’ ”

He effectively agreed with the protesters but went on to interpret their language of human rights in a very particular way. It was truly a scandal, he argued, that UN human rights covenants “offer no effective protection of economic freedoms, property rights and rule of law.”

Even as he sought to ground WTO in human rights language, he sought to insert economic language into dominant human rights talk. “The traditional disregard in WTO law of human rights is becoming as outdated as the persistent disregard in international human rights instruments for economic liberty and freedom of trade as preconditions for individual welfare.”

zh: 彼得斯曼1997年曾盛赞为哈耶克式宪政设计之凯旋的那项协定，到2001年已被他斥为存在这样的弊病：“世贸组织成员国的许多国家议会，在几个小时内便批准了两万五千页的乌拉圭回合协定，既无正当的议会审查，也无透明的讨论。”
尽管用他自己的话说，“从宪政角度看，从1947年关贸总协定到世贸组织的过渡，提供了国际贸易法‘宪政化’成功的一个范例”，但它在实践中正归于失败。
人们在世贸组织身上看到的核心问题，按照其他法学家的说法，是“缺乏一个正当的、足以产生正当性的目的”。
这彻底的反转令人着迷——民主压力的缺席本身，如今竟被视为该机构的阿喀琉斯之踵。看来，制度设计终究无法消除对民主正当性的需要。
en: The agreement that Petersmann had praised in 1997 as a triumph of Hayekian constitutional design was, by 2001, disparaged for the fact that “many national parliaments in WTO member countries ratified the 25,000 pages of the Uruguay Round Agreements within a few hours without proper parliamentary review and transparent discussion.”

Even though, as he put it, “from a constitutional perspective, the transition from GATT 1947 to the WTO offers an example of a successful ‘constitutionalization’ of international trade law,” it was becoming a failure in practice.
The central problem people saw in the WTO was, as other legal scholars see it, “the absence of a legitimate and legitimating purpose.”
The about-face was fascinating—the very absence of democratic pressures was now being seen as an Achilles’ heel of the institution. Democratic legitimacy, it seemed, could not be designed away.

zh: 彼得斯曼本人针对正当性难题开出的药方，是进一步加码对人权的强调。他把人权宣称为开展行动的新领域：“继1989年‘草根民主革命’之后，”他写道，“经济与法律全球化（包括世贸组织的全球一体化法律）提供了再掀一场‘人权革命’的可能，以利于非歧视的开放市场、全球竞争与更有效的人权保护。”
以一种别出心裁的解读，他把“阿拉伯之春”的一系列反抗读作正是这样一场要求商业权利与市场权利的革命。

与早先形态的日内瓦学派新自由主义不同——后者常把个人视为破坏性的政治行动者——多层级宪政主义的版本敞开了个人自下而上发挥积极政治作用的可能。在那些谴责世贸组织是脱离群众的遥远官僚机构的声音中，在那些追踪新自由主义世界规划之变异的人那里，这一角度常常被漏看。哈耶克曾呼吁“政治退位”，而2000年的日内瓦学派谈的却是政治的再配置：把市场公民身份及其主张，视为从个人层面直至世界层面把全球体系编织起来的方式。彼得斯曼在西雅图之后写道：“公民参与世贸组织的协商机构与其他多层级的国际治理机制，能够增强世界贸易体制的正当性与政治支持。”
en: Petersmann’s own solution for the legitimacy problem was to ramp up the emphasis on human rights. He claimed human rights as a new frontier for activism: “Following the ‘democratic grass-root revolution of 1989,’ ” he wrote, “economic and legal globalization (including the global integration law of the WTO) offer the possibility for another ‘human rights revolution’ in favor of non-discriminatory open markets, global competition and more effective protection of human rights.”
In an idiosyncratic interpretation, he read the string of revolts in the Arab Spring as part of just such a revolutionary demand for business and market rights.

Unlike the earlier form of Geneva School neoliberalism, which often saw the individual as a disruptive political actor, the multilevel constitutionalist version opened the possibility of a positive bottom-up political role for individuals. This is an angle often missed in the denunciations of the WTO as a detached distant bureaucracy and by those seeking to track the mutations of the neoliberal world project. Whereas Hayek had called for the “dethronement of politics,” the Geneva School of the year 2000 was talking about a reconfiguration of politics, seeing market citizenship and its claims as the way in which the global system could be knit together from the level of the individual to the world. Petersmann wrote after Seattle, “Citizen participation in consultative WTO bodies and other multi-levelled international governance mechanisms could strengthen the legitimacy and political support for the world trading system.”

zh: 有学者指出：“与大多数人不同，市场即便不被热爱，也能运转得相当好。”
但完全相反的情形或许才是真的。许多人得不到爱也照样活下去；而经验表明，对某一秩序的正当性给予某种程度的关切，是该秩序不致滑向混乱与民众反抗所必需的。市场若不被热爱，就需要被接受。“以公民为中心”这一面的重要性，常被那些只把新自由主义宪法“仅仅视为给国家权威设限的手段”的学者所忽视。
方程式的正面是存在的——那就是贸易的权利。一位批评者称，彼得斯曼的这一路径是企图“劫持——或者更恰当地说，‘哈耶克’（Hayek）——国际人权法”。
彼得斯曼所提出的，正是一种自下而上的解决方案之可能性。
en: One scholar notes that “unlike most people, a market can function quite well without being loved.”

But the exact reverse might be true. Many people persist without love, and experience has shown that some attention to the legitimacy of a given order is necessary for it not to descend into chaos and popular revolt. If not loved, the market needs to be accepted. The importance of the “citizen-centered” aspect is often overlooked by scholars who see the neoliberal constitution “solely as a means to impose limits on state authorities.”

The positive side of the equation exists—it is the right to trade. One critic called this approach an attempt by Petersmann “to hijack, or more appropriately to Hayek, international human rights law.”
Petersmann was proposing the possibility of a fix from below.

zh: 然而，自下而上的解决方案在实践中究竟是什么模样？日内瓦学派的设想——个人越过本国向更高层面申诉，或在本国之内诉诸世界法，从而加固治理结构的正当性——迄今基本只有公司在走这条路。请不起一支贸易律师团队——其人数自1990年代以来呈指数级增长——到头来便成了跻身这种市场公民身份的门槛。贸易协定（如世贸组织协定）的谈判者们，绝非超然于众、不受特殊利益俘获的立法者（nomothetes），他们与企业游说团体保持着密切而正式的关系。例如，美国的“私营部门咨询程序”由三十多个委员会组成，吸纳近一千名私营部门人士定期开会，就世界贸易的法律架构需要向他们提供什么，向美国贸易代表进言。
彼得斯曼所描述的那种“自下而上”正当化的现实版本，纳入的只是世界经济市场公民中的少数一部分。
en: Yet what does the fix from below look like in practice? The Geneva School idea of individuals reinforcing the legitimacy of the governing structures by appealing above their own nations, or to world law within their nations, has been a path taken largely by corporations only. An inability to pay a team of trade lawyers—whose numbers have grown exponentially since the 1990s—ends up being a bar to entering this form of market citizenship. Far from being detached nomothetes above the possibility of capture by special interests, the negotiators of trade agreements like the WTO have close and formal relationships with corporate lobbies. The “private sector advisory process” in the United States, for example, comprised over thirty committees, involving nearly one thousand individuals from the private sector, that met regularly to advise the U.S. trade representative on what they needed from the legal architecture of world trade.
The actual existing version of the “bottom-up” legitimation described by Petersmann included only a select slice of the world economy’s market citizens.

zh: 作为西雅图之后重塑品牌的一部分，世贸组织修复了旧画——1970年代末关贸总协定初次迁入威廉·拉帕德中心（Centre William Rappard）中国际劳工组织的办公地时，那些画曾被遮盖、挪走。展现劳动者在劳动与休闲中英姿的壁画重见天日。
2012年，彼得斯曼端详楼身，发出疑问：为什么他在世贸组织工作的十六年间，没有人对入口处的两尊雕像说过一句话——那是“和平”与“正义”的寓意像。

只字未提的一点——他肯定心知肚明——是这两尊雕像乃国际劳工组织时代的遗物。雇员或谈判代表们对雕像视若无睹，并不奇怪。世贸组织的使命不是实现和平或正义，而是锁定自由贸易规则，校准多层级政体，容许针对价格信号作出永续调适。对于彼得斯曼的导师哈耶克而言，唯一可允许的正义形式，就是不论历史、平等对待所有参与者的程序正义。一旦正义与社会正义之义的公平配对——如国际劳工组织的使命所定，或如拉米的日内瓦共识所提——正义就不只是用错了地方，还会造成危害。社会正义是一种要求以既定目标支配社会的主张，为极权主义铺路；它是一种返祖的痉挛，要把人类从扩展秩序与大社会拽回到“部落社会”。
en: As part of their post-Seattle rebranding, the WTO restored the old paintings that had been covered and removed when the GATT first moved into the offices of the International Labour Organization at the Centre William Rappard in the late 1970s. Murals showing heroic workers in acts of labor and leisure once again saw the light of day.

In 2012 Petersmann looked at the building himself and asked why nobody in his sixteen years working at the WTO had commented on the two statues at the entrance—allegorical figures of “peace” and “justice.”

Unmentioned was the fact, which he would have surely known, that the statues were relics of the days of the ILO. The failure of employees or negotiators to remark on the statues was no mystery. WTO’s mandate was not to achieve peace or justice but to lock in liberal trade rules to calibrate multilevel polities and allow for perpetual adjustment in response to price signals. For Petersmann’s mentor, Hayek, the only permissible form of justice was procedural justice that treated all participants equally regardless of history. When paired with equity as social justice as in the mandate of the ILO—or in Lamy’s Geneva Consensus—justice was worse than a non sequitur. Social justice was a teleocratic demand that paved the way to totalitarianism, and an atavistic spasm sending humanity from the extended order and Great Society back to the “tribal society.”

zh: 彼得斯曼对历史的取舍式阅读，在他对自己2012年出版的著作封面的解说中再度显露。封面用的是墨西哥画家迭戈·里维拉（Diego Rivera）的《卖马蹄莲的女子》（Calla Lily Vendor，1941），画中一名女子被一座美丽白花堆成的山压弯了腰。他在正文中称之为“在市场上自由出售商品”的象征。
里维拉是正式的共产党员，最以礼赞劳工的壁画闻名——这一点丝毫未能阻止彼得斯曼对里维拉作品的歪曲利用，以强化他自己那套把市场权利视为最基本人权的信念。
拉米为其日内瓦共识之书选得更贴切：一幅装饰世贸组织墙面的新画作，让-克洛德·普雷特尔（Jean-Claude Prêtre）的《达那厄世界组曲》（
World Suite，2001）。画面呈现一幅墨卡托投影的世界，其上覆以十字交叉的网格与斑斓的漆点。大陆的轮廓在网格之下几乎难以辨识。这幅画让人更接近这个机构赖以建立的观念。尽管近来转而使用人权话语，它终究是这样一种世界经济观念：几乎无法加以再现，处于永恒的变形与流转之中，被一张规则之网围封。
en: Petersmann’s selective reading of history was displayed again in his gloss on the cover of a book he published in 2012. The cover featured Mexican painter Diego Rivera’s
(1941), depicting a woman bowed under the weight of a mountain of beautiful white flowers. In the text, he called it an icon of “the freedom to sell in the market place.”

The fact that Rivera was a card-carrying Communist best known for his workerist murals was no obstacle to Petersmann’s misrepresentation of Rivera’s work to reinforce his own dedication to market rights as the most fundamental of human rights.
A more fitting choice was made by Lamy for his book on the Geneva Consensus: one of the newer paintings that decorated the WTO’s walls, from the

by Jean-Claude Prêtre. The painting shows a Mercator projection of the world beneath a grid of crosses and flecks of colorful paint. Barely visible underneath are the outlines of the continents. The image suggests something closer to what the institution was built on. Notwithstanding the late conversion to a language of human rights, it is a conception of the world economy at the edges of representation, in a perpetual state of morphing and transformation, encased by a grid of rules.

zh: 倘若彼得斯曼从威廉·拉帕德中心越过十英尺高的金属路障和持枪守卫，望向街对面的环岛，就会看到一样东西——比那幅里维拉的画更难被重新解释成贸易而非劳动的象征。这座纪念碑建于1937年——正是哈耶克发表《经济学与知识》、罗宾斯刊发其反计划宣言、李普曼（Lippmann）出版《善的社会》（The Good Society）的那一年——用以纪念国际劳工组织的创始人阿尔贝·托马（Albert Thomas）。基座上是劳动的群像：煤矿工在煤壁前刨挖，渔民在海上作业，农民在耕作与搬运收获物。顶端的四个人像，一位是戴圆帽、端米筛的亚洲男子，一位是披兜帽、负皮毛的土著男子，一位是身着工装围裙、手握钳子的工人，还有一位是手执锄头的非洲黑人男子。基座上镌刻着难以曲解的话：“劳动高于一切竞争角逐。劳动不是商品。”小规模的抗议不时在此集会。2005年，来自五大洲的抗议者在此举行示威，一名巴西妇女发表了关于“反对资本主义的斗争”的演说。一条横幅喊出的，正是新自由主义者当初组织起来反对的那个世界：“建设一个团结的世界。”
en: Had Petersmann looked across the street from the Centre William Rappard past the ten-foot metal barriers and armed guards, in the traffic circle, he would have seen something that would be more difficult than the Rivera painting to transform from labor into trade. Erected in 1937, the year Hayek published his essay “Economics and Knowledge,” Robbins his deplanning manifesto, and Lippmann

the monument commemorated the ILO’s founder, Albert Thomas. The base shows images of work: miners picking at a coalface, fishers at sea, farmers tilling and hauling crops. The four figures on top are a skull-capped Asian man carrying a rice sieve, a hooded indigenous man carrying pelts, a man in worker’s apron holding pincers, and a black African man with a hoe. Etched into the plinth are words difficult to spin: “Labor exists above all struggles for competition. It is not a commodity.” Small protests assemble here. In 2005 a demonstration of protesters from five continents gathered there and a Brazilian woman gave a speech about the “struggle against capitalism.” One of the banners suggested the very world against which the neoliberals had organized: “Building a world of solidarity.”

zh: 1990年代是新自由主义全球主义作为制度建设工程的高峰。在那个没完没了的全球化话语的十年里，“世界经济”被授予凌驾于任何单一国家之上的权力。政客们习惯于搬出世界经济作挡箭牌，为削减福利与结构调整辩护——有一个超国家的惩戒者可供他们一边歉意地指指点点、一边耸肩摊手，实在方便；他们在砍去战后和解方案的又一项条件时，便如此这般推诿。归咎于世界经济是一种可持续的策略，因为这个惩戒者只是它的两副政治面孔之一。在它的另一副面孔下，世界经济被召唤为一只丰饶之角，里面盛满买得起的消费品，由一股廉价信贷的溪流浇灌。这一策略的凶险直到2000年代初、尤其是2008年之后才暴露无遗。当世界经济不再给予，它脸上剩下的便只有替罪羊的面具。选民的回应在意料之中：投票反对它。
en: The 1990s were the high point of neoliberal globalism as an institution-building project. In the decade’s endless globalization talk, “the world economy” was granted a power beyond any single nation. Politicians grew accustomed to deferring to the world economy to justify cuts to welfare benefits and restructuring. It was convenient to have an extranational disciplinarian to which they could gesture apologetically and shrug as they shaved off another condition of the postwar settlement. Blaming the world economy was a sustainable strategy because the disciplinarian was only one of its two political faces. In its inverse incarnation, the world economy was summoned as a cornucopia of affordable consumer goods irrigated by a stream of cheap credit. The perils of this strategy were made clear only in the early 2000s and especially after 2008. When the world economy stopped giving, it was left wearing only the mask of the scapegoat. Voters reacted predictably: by voting against it.

zh: 或许可以认为，日内瓦学派的新自由主义者到头来成了制度决定论者——尽管这全然出于其本意之外。尽管他们时常声称信奉“自下而上的自由主义”，信奉勒普克所谓文化价值的腐殖土，但这些自称“反计划者”对二十世纪最持久的智识贡献，或许恰恰就是他们的蓝图与计划。也许，日内瓦学派的新自由主义者忙着为世界经济修筑水晶堡垒，竟未曾听从米塞斯的劝告——去加固那种让大众相信，应当把全球市场而非一国市场视为一种无条件的善，而非可以随境况好坏取舍的实用选择。他们没有为下行期做出任何预案，也从未想出安抚被巨大的不平等分裂的民众的办法。对他们来说幸运的是，资本主义的安康并不依赖——也从未依赖——他们的干预。但倘若日内瓦学派的新自由主义者把民众对自由贸易全球主义的拥戴看作众多特征中居于核心且不可或缺的一项，那么他们在21世纪初就有理由忧心忡忡了。以上篇章，讲的就是通往当前危机的漫漫长路。
en: One could argue that Geneva School neoliberals ended up being institutional determinists in spite of themselves. Though often claiming a commitment to “liberalism from below” and the need for what Röpke called the humus of cultural values, the most enduring intellectual contribution of these purported “anti-planners” to the twentieth century may have been their blueprints and plans. It may be that Geneva School neoliberals were so busy building crystalline fortresses for the world economy that they failed to heed Mises’s advice about reinforcing a mass mentality that would favor global rather than national markets as an absolute good rather than a pragmatic good to be favored or rejected as fortunes changed. They did not plan for the downturn, nor did they ever figure out a way to placate populations cleft by vast gaps of inequality. Luckily for them, the well-being of capitalism does not rely on their interventions, and never had. But if Geneva School neoliberals saw a popular commitment to free-trade globalism as not just one feature of many but the central necessary feature, then they would have reason to worry in the early twenty-first century. These pages have told the story of the long road to the current crisis.

zh: 诊断出新自由主义的危机，并不等于说经济不平等已停止加剧；也不等于说把市场方案套用于社会问题、以金钱衡量一切人的价值的做法已经停摆；更不等于说我们见证了再分配模式的回归，或向凯恩斯式福利国家意识形态的转向。国家吸纳私人债务与量化宽松政策，并未扭转“私人凯恩斯主义”的长期现实——正是它加剧着巨富阶层与其余人等之间的鸿沟。
en: To diagnose a crisis of neoliberalism is not to suggest that economic inequality has ceased to advance. Nor that the application of market solutions to social problems or the calculation of all human value in monetary terms has ceased, nor that we have witnessed a return to a pattern of redistribution or a turn to Keynesian welfare state ideology. The state absorption of private debt and policies of quantitative easing have not reversed the long-standing realities of “private Keynesianism” that ex-acerbate the gap between the hyperwealthy and the rest.

zh: 然而，自世贸组织创建以来就一直困扰它的正当性危机表明，作为一种独特新自由主义支脉的秩序全球主义，或许已经越出了自己的极限。如果说目标是精细调校规则，以防社会正义或再分配的扰攘要求，那么胜利遥不可及。新兴国家要求美国和欧洲兑现其自由贸易主张，以美国未曾预料的方式运用世贸组织，造成全球僵局。这遥相呼应了1958年哈伯勒报告之后的行动。
其他国家已开始拒绝那些旨在为外国投资者确立异邦人权（xenos rights）的双边投资条约。
一本新近的书谈的是“后新自由主义的世界贸易法”。
对平等的要求——有时以包容的方式表达，有时以排斥的方式表达——持续搅动着政治版图，反抗一切试图引入形式平等、却否认历史上形成的现实不平等的努力。
en: Yet the legitimacy crises that have plagued the WTO since its creation suggest that ordoglobalism as a distinct strain of neoliberalism may have overreached. If the goal was to fine-tune the rules to prevent disruptive demands for social justice or redistribution, then victory is nowhere in sight. In a late echo of the activism following the 1958 Haberler Report, emerging countries have created global gridlock by demanding that the United States and Europe live up to their own free-trade rhetoric, thereby using the WTO in ways that the United States itself had not anticipated.
Other nations have begun rejecting the bilateral investment treaties designed to lock in xenos rights for foreign investors.
One recent book writes of “world trade law after neoliberalism.”

Demands for evenness, sometimes expressed in inclusionary and sometimes in exclusionary ways, continue to roil the political landscape against all attempts to introduce a formal equality that disavows historically determined real inequality.

zh: 新自由主义者抨击社会主义者梦想一个没有输家的世界经济，但他们自己同样梦想一个没有规则破坏者的世界经济——更重要的，是梦想一个没有理想主义——在他们看来即返祖——的规则破坏者结盟的世界经济，因为后者图谋改变那套激励、义务与回报的体系。2010年代中期，支持脱欧的全民公投获胜，具有约束力的贸易立法日渐失宠，这都表明：即便新自由主义者的意图是“撤销人民”，无论此事是好是坏，人民尚未被取消。
en: Neoliberals criticize socialists for their dream of a world economy without losers, but they had their own dream of a world economy without rule breakers and more importantly without idealistic—or, in their opinion, atavistic—alliances of rule breakers who seek to change the system of incentives, obligations, and rewards. In the mid-2010s, the popular referendum in favor of Brexit and the declining popularity of binding trade legislation suggests that even if the intentions of the neoliberals was to “undo the demos,” the demos—for better or for worse—is not undone yet.
